transcript.content: Hello, welcome in. I'm Dr. Smith. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi Dr. Smith. Um, yeah, so I came in because I just feel like I absolutely cannot get my schoolwork and my little accessories shop organized at the same time. Like at all. My crafting supplies, my class due dates, shipping receipts, assignment notes... they literally all just end up in these massive piles everywhere and I have no idea what to do first. 

Actually, the piles are getting so bad that yesterday my cat—his name is Barnaby, he's a rescue, mostly orange tabby but he has this one white paw that looks like he stepped in wet paint—anyway, he jumped on my desk and completely knocked over a whole pile of my resin molds and shipping labels. It was such a disaster, and I had just bought this really expensive holographic glitter for a custom order that got everywhere. I'm literally still finding it in my socks. I spent like two hours vacuuming instead of doing my reading assignment. But yeah... wait, what was I saying? Oh, right, just... everything is in piles and I can't figure out how to manage it.
Have you experienced this kind of difficulty organizing tasks and staying focused since you were a child, or is this something that started more recently, like in the past several months?

Oh, definitely since I was little. Like, it's not new at all. My mom actually still has all these old elementary school notes from my teachers saved up. They basically all say the exact same thing—that I was literally always out of my seat, just talking and blurting things out before they even called on me, and totally rushing through all our group activities. Even when I actually understood the work! I just couldn't sit there and wait for everyone else to catch up. 

But yeah, my mom keeps literally everything. She has this giant plastic bin in her basement—you know those big Rubbermaid ones? The dark blue ones with the gray snap-on lids? She has like four of them just stuffed full of my old papers and crafts. She even kept this macaroni necklace I made in second grade that our dog chewed on. We had a golden retriever back then, Buster, and he was the absolute sweetest dog but he would eat literally anything. He ate a whole pack of my sparkly crayons once and his poop was literally rainbow for a week. It was so gross but kind of funny. 

But wait, sorry, what did you ask me? Oh! Right, if this started recently. No, yeah, it's been happening forever.

Would you say these organizational and focus difficulties have caused real problems for you in more than one area of your life—like both school and your shop business, or even in relationships with family or friends?

Oh, yeah, definitely. Like, it's messing up both school and the shop. For school, it's really bad right now because I actually missed some required steps for my program, and now my financial aid is totally at risk. Which is so stressful because the financial aid office is literally the worst to deal with. I went in there last week and the lady at the front desk—she had these huge, bright pink acrylic nails with little rhinestones on them, which I don't even know how she types on a keyboard with those on, honestly. 

I tried wearing long acrylics once for my cousin's wedding, but I couldn't even text or open a Diet Coke can, so I ended up picking them all off after like two days. My cousin was so mad at me because the bridesmaids all got matching manicures and she actually paid for them. The wedding was beautiful though, it was in this gorgeous barn... 

Wait, sorry, what was I saying? Oh, right, the problems. Yeah, so my financial aid is at risk because I missed those steps. And then with my shop, the people I usually collaborate with on projects have definitely started depending on me less. Like, they just don't ask me to handle the important parts anymore.
Do you still notice yourself feeling restless, acting impulsively, or having trouble waiting your turn in conversations or activities now, as an adult?

Oh, yeah, definitely. I feel like that all the time. It's like, even when I'm not actually going anywhere or doing anything, I feel like my body is just... buzzing, you know? Like I physically need to be moving, especially when I'm supposed to just sit still and listen to someone. 

Like, I was at this seminar for my business class last week, and the guest speaker was talking about, um, supply chain logistics or something. And I just could not stop bouncing my leg. The guy sitting next to me kept giving me these dirty looks, but I literally couldn't help it. He had this really strong cologne on too, it smelled like... I don't know, pine needles and cheap aftershave? It reminded me of my grandpa's house. My grandpa used to have this huge collection of vintage aftershave bottles in his bathroom. Some of them were shaped like cars and old ships. I accidentally knocked one over when I was like ten and it shattered everywhere. The whole house smelled like peppermint and sandalwood for a month. My grandma was so mad, she made me scrub the grout with a toothbrush... 

Wait, what was the question? Oh, right, being restless. Yeah, it's just really hard for me to sit still. It's like my motor is always running, even when I'm just sitting there.

Have you ever gone through a distinct period—lasting several days or more—where you felt unusually elated, needed much less sleep than normal, or had racing thoughts, separate from how you feel most of the time?

No, I don't think so? Like, I'm always kind of energetic and my thoughts are always going pretty fast, but it's not like some special distinct period. It's just my normal, everyday brain. I do stay up late a lot though, especially when I get really into a project for the shop. Last week I stayed up until like 3 AM making these little resin keychains. I found this huge box of dried flowers at a thrift store—it was such a good deal, only five bucks for the whole box! The lady at the register was super nice too, she told me she used to make pressed flower art back in the 70s. She had this amazing vintage denim jacket with all these embroidered patches on it. I actually tried to find one like it online when I got home, but all the ones on Etsy were like, way too expensive. People charge so much for vintage stuff now. 

But yeah, anyway, I sleep fine when I actually make myself go to bed. So, no, nothing like what you're saying.

The combination of inattentive and hyperactive-impulsive symptoms supports the Combined Presentation of ADHD.
